name: Azeroth Unbound
author: NeedleDropper
description: A Death Stranding-style needle-drop soundtrack for World of Warcraft: Forever's open world. One song the first time you arrive in every zone and capital, plus a handful of iconic landmarks: melancholy, spacious post-rock, indie folk and ambient electronica for cresting a hill and seeing somewhere new. Metadata only; no audio is included.

drops.title: The Wolves (Act I and II)
drops.note: Red rock, hot wind and a people newly freed: a hushed, slowly swelling lament for wolf riders who are only now learning what home means.

drops.title: Birthplace
drops.note: The tauren's cradle of golden grass and slow rivers deserves a song literally named for where you were born.

drops.title: Awake
drops.note: A new lookout high above the plains of Mulgore, named for watching the sky: warm, wide-open sunlight in song form.

drops.title: Your Hand in Mine
drops.note: An endless savanna under a huge sky; the guitars build and recede like heat over the road to the Crossroads. Plays a 6:30 excerpt of the 8:17 track.

drops.title: Near Light
drops.note: Moonlight filtered through the World Tree's canopy: piano, strings and a soft electronic pulse that glow rather than shine.

drops.title: Sæglópur
drops.note: The title means 'lost at sea', and Darkshore is a grey, mournful coast full of shipwrecks and drowned ruins. Plays a 6:30 excerpt of the 7:38 track.

drops.title: The Light
drops.note: Ancient twilight forest where shafts of light still break through the canopy, even as the axes of war bite at its edge.

drops.title: Asylums for the Feeling
drops.note: A Death Stranding needle drop (with Leila Adu on vocals) for a landscape that could be from it: towering mesas, a long way down, and a lot of quiet. Plays a 6:30 excerpt of the 7:09 track.

drops.title: Esja
drops.note: Named for a mountain over Reykjavík; climbing piano for the high, wind-cut peaks above the logging scars.

drops.title: Don't Be So Serious
drops.note: A grey, bone-strewn wasteland of kodo graveyards and warring centaur, scored by Low Roar at their most weary and tender.

drops.title: Mystery of Love
drops.note: Humid summer light, overgrown elven ruins and giant trees: a lush, aching song for a forgotten corner of the world.

drops.title: Daydreaming
drops.note: Fog over black water and a city at the edge of everything; this song drifts and loops like the marsh itself.

drops.title: A Shimmer
drops.note: Dunes wavering in the heat haze, with the Caverns of Time somewhere beyond them: a spare upright-piano piece whose title says the rest.

drops.title: Maria También
drops.note: A walled goblin market in the middle of the desert, scored with a sun-baked, bazaar-flavoured groove.

drops.title: Wait
drops.note: An eternal autumn coast of ruined Highborne palaces; a gentle, dream-heavy song about a glamour that is already gone.

drops.title: The Curse
drops.note: A forest poisoned from the roots up, and a song titled for exactly that.

drops.title: Emerald Rush
drops.note: Primeval green, hot springs and dinosaurs: a pulsing, overgrown rush of a track for the crater floor.

drops.title: To Build a Home
drops.note: A camp clinging to a cliff in a prehistoric world: a song about the fragile shelters we make.

drops.title: An Ending (Ascent)
drops.note: The druids' sanctuary is the one place no war reaches; Eno's slow ascent is pure stillness.

drops.title: Northern Sky
drops.note: The druid village by the moonlit lake, greeted with a warm, glowing love song under a northern sky.

drops.title: Heptapod B
drops.note: Something alien lives under these dunes; Jóhannsson's choir-and-drone piece from Arrival makes the hives feel vast and unknowable.

drops.title: Easy Way Out
drops.note: A lonely druid outpost holding the line against the swarm; Low Roar's weary hope for people who refuse to leave.

drops.title: Holocene
drops.note: Snowfields so wide they make you feel small, which is exactly what this song is about.

drops.title: White Winter Hymnal
drops.note: A warm goblin town in the snowfields, greeted by a round of voices singing about winter.

drops.title: Ludens
drops.note: Iron spikes, war drums and a city built in defiance; the loudest Death Stranding song for the loudest capital.

drops.title: Go Do
drops.note: Drums, flutes and wind high on the mesas: a joyful, primal call that fits the tauren's city above the clouds.

drops.title: Runaway
drops.note: A temple city of moonwells and owls; an ethereal Nordic song about longing for a home far away.

drops.title: Outro
drops.note: The climb toward Nordrassil, where the world was once saved, earns the biggest swell in the pack.

drops.title: To the Wilder
drops.note: A brand-new land of Highborne exiles and centaur plains, scored with a Death Stranding 2 song about heading out into the unknown.

drops.title: Helvegen
drops.note: Snow, pine and the bones of a traitor kingdom; a Norse lament for the road to the dead. Plays a 6:30 excerpt of the 7:11 track.

drops.title: Glass
drops.note: The city of mages sealed under a violet dome, seen from outside like something behind glass.

drops.title: Welcome, Ghosts
drops.note: Windswept highlands, standing stones and the ruins of Stromgarde: post-rock that rises like weather over open hills, with a title that greets the ghosts of the first human kingdom.

drops.title: Paris, Texas
drops.note: Sun-bleached canyons and dragon bones; Ry Cooder's slide guitar is the sound of walking alone through a dry country.

drops.title: Bridge of Death
drops.note: A red wasteland poisoned by the magic that tore open the Dark Portal; Guðnadóttir's Chernobyl score is the sound of an invisible catastrophe still falling from the sky.

drops.title: Bones
drops.note: You wake up dead in a gloomy glade; Low Roar's Death Stranding song about what remains is the Forsaken's first breath.

drops.title: In a Week
drops.note: A dark folk duet about lying still in the woods long after it is over, for a pine forest full of the dead and the hunted.

drops.title: The Last of Us
drops.note: Abandoned farmsteads and overgrown fields after the plague: a lonely guitar theme from the defining post-apocalyptic game.

drops.title: On the Nature of Daylight
drops.note: The heart of the blight, where Stratholme burned; Richter's strings are grief with nowhere left to go.

drops.title: Hoppípolla
drops.note: The last bastion of light in the plague, and the moment of pure hope that the blight has not taken everything.

drops.title: Passing Afternoon
drops.note: Orchards, farmland and a quiet war between two villages; a gentle song with something sad underneath.

drops.title: An Ocean and a Rock
drops.note: A small seaside town clinging to the coast, with a small, tender song about the sea.

drops.title: Blue Ridge Mountains
drops.note: Wild forested hills, gryphons overhead and a long way from anywhere: Appalachian harmonies for the Hinterlands.

drops.title: King and Cross
drops.note: Icelandic snow-pop for the first snowfall of a dwarf or gnome's life.

drops.title: Open Eye Signal
drops.note: Molten rivers and Dark Iron slave pits; a relentless, machine-like pulse for a land that never stops working. Plays a 6:30 excerpt of the 7:48 track.

drops.title: Quiet
drops.note: Ash falling without a sound on the scorched plains under Blackrock: the song keeps to its title for as long as it can, then the guitars catch fire.

drops.title: I'll Keep Coming
drops.note: The first needle drop: the most iconic Death Stranding song for the quiet, golden forest where so many journeys begin.

drops.title: Flight from the City
drops.note: Dead trees, endless wind and Karazhan looming; a slow piano piece that feels like walking away from something you cannot unsee.

drops.title: Hunted by a Freak
drops.note: Eternal night, worgen in the trees and a graveyard on the hill; the title alone says it, and the song never quite lets you relax.

drops.title: Stay Alive
drops.note: A calm highland lake behind a great dam, scored with the song from The Secret Life of Walter Mitty's own northern wanderings.

drops.title: Ends of the Earth
drops.note: The first time the road leaves Elwynn behind: a wanderlust song for red cliffs, a lake town and the open road east.

drops.title: Kiara
drops.note: Dense, humid jungle full of overgrown troll ruins; a lush, melancholy electronic track with a heartbeat.

drops.title: Elephant Gun
drops.note: A pirate town in a skull-shaped cove: Balkan brass, ukulele and a song that sways like a ship.

drops.title: Riverside
drops.note: A drowned temple and a swamp named for grief: a spare piano song about going down to the water alone.

drops.title: The Stable Song
drops.note: Abandoned farms, broken windmills and dust: a song from a man who actually farms, about what is left behind.

drops.title: Anchor
drops.note: Rain, mud and the grey sea at Menethil; a hushed falsetto song with the weight of rain in it.

drops.title: Old Pine
drops.note: A harbour of departures across the sea; a song of youth, fires on the beach and leaving.

drops.title: King and Lionheart
drops.note: The city of the lion and its kings, greeted with an Icelandic anthem that marches in like a parade.

drops.title: Iron
drops.note: Into the mountain, past the Great Forge: Woodkid's brass and war drums for the city literally made of iron.

drops.title: Goodbye
drops.note: A city of the dead beneath the ruins of a fallen kingdom; a funeral-slow song famous from the series Dark.

drops.title: Árbakkinn
drops.note: 'Árbakkinn' is Icelandic for 'the riverbank': a spoken poem over piano for a brand-new land of rivers and contested glades.

drops.title: Blurred
drops.note: A goblin port on a lit fuse: crisp, ticking electronics that slowly build to the bang.

drops.title: Dayvan Cowboy
drops.note: A floating island in the plane of air: a song forever tied to a record-breaking fall from the edge of space.
